prompt:
--- Design document ---
Limited-edition drop: stock reservation design (design doc)

The shop has 4 units of a limited-edition item in stock, and 5 customers (c1, c2, c3, c4, c5) try to buy
it at the same time. Each customer's checkout runs on its own server thread; the threads interleave
arbitrarily. A checkout first reserves a unit (a hold), then the customer pays to confirm the
purchase.

Holds are temporary: a hold that is not paid for expires after 4 clock ticks, and the unit goes
back into stock so that another customer can buy it. Customers can be slow to pay; the payment step
may happen at any later time.

Reserving. The checkout thread reads the current stock count from the database, checks that it is
above zero, and then, as a separate statement, writes back the count it read minus one. No lock or
transaction spans the read and the write.

Paying. The payment service confirms an order only if the customer's hold is still active; payment
for an expired hold is refused and the customer must start again.

Initially all customers are browsing and the stock count is 4.

--- Event model ---
The possible events in this system are modelled by the following STRIPS planning domain. Each action
is one event; it can happen only when its precondition holds, and its effect updates the state
(closed world: facts not stated are false).

```pddl
(define (domain inventory)
  (:requirements :strips :typing)
  (:types customer level tick)
  (:predicates
    ;; --- design facts (which of these hold depends on the design) ---
    (mode-1)
    (mode-4)
    (mode-3)
    (mode-2)
    ;; --- static counters ---
    (next-level ?lower ?higher - level)  ; stock level ?higher is one more than ?lower
    (zero-tick ?t - tick)
    (next-tick ?t ?u - tick)
    (hold-limit ?t - tick)               ; hold age at which a hold expires
    ;; --- state ---
    (stock ?q - level)                   ; current stock level
    (browsing ?c - customer)             ; customer has not started checkout
    (read-1 ?c - customer ?q - level)
    (holding ?c - customer)              ; customer holds one reserved unit
    (hold-age ?c - customer ?t - tick)
    (expired ?c - customer)              ; customer's hold expired and its unit went back to stock
    (sold ?c - customer))                ; customer's purchase is confirmed

  (:action read-1
    :parameters (?c - customer ?q ?p - level)
    :precondition (and (mode-1) (browsing ?c) (stock ?q) (next-level ?p ?q))
    :effect (and (not (browsing ?c)) (read-1 ?c ?q)))
  (:action write-stock
    :parameters (?c - customer ?q ?p ?cur - level ?t - tick)
    :precondition (and (read-1 ?c ?q) (next-level ?p ?q) (stock ?cur) (zero-tick ?t))
    :effect (and (not (read-1 ?c ?q)) (not (stock ?cur)) (stock ?p) (holding ?c) (hold-age ?c ?t)))
  (:action reserve-1
    :parameters (?c - customer ?q ?p - level ?t - tick)
    :precondition (and (mode-4) (browsing ?c) (stock ?q) (next-level ?p ?q) (zero-tick ?t))
    :effect (and (not (browsing ?c)) (not (stock ?q)) (stock ?p) (holding ?c) (hold-age ?c ?t)))
  (:action hold-ages
    :parameters (?c - customer ?t ?u - tick)
    :precondition (and (holding ?c) (hold-age ?c ?t) (next-tick ?t ?u))
    :effect (and (not (hold-age ?c ?t)) (hold-age ?c ?u)))
  (:action expire-hold
    :parameters (?c - customer ?t - tick ?q ?r - level)
    :precondition (and (holding ?c) (hold-age ?c ?t) (hold-limit ?t) (stock ?q) (next-level ?q ?r))
    :effect (and (not (holding ?c)) (not (hold-age ?c ?t)) (not (stock ?q)) (stock ?r) (expired ?c)))
  (:action pay
    :parameters (?c - customer ?t - tick)
    :precondition (and (holding ?c) (hold-age ?c ?t))
    :effect (and (not (holding ?c)) (not (hold-age ?c ?t)) (sold ?c)))
  (:action pay-1
    :parameters (?c - customer)
    :precondition (and (mode-2) (expired ?c))
    :effect (and (not (expired ?c)) (sold ?c))))
```

Object names: customers c1 to c5; stock levels q0 (empty) to q4; hold ages t0 to t4.

Question: Can every one of the customers end up with a confirmed purchase, i.e. more items sold than were in stock? In the event model this means reaching a state where (and (sold c1) (sold c2) (sold c3) (sold c4) (sold c5)) holds.

Every action's precondition must hold at the moment it occurs. If it cannot happen under this design,

# Pre-mortem Analysis: Limited-edition Drop Stock Reservation

I need to find a concrete event sequence that causes all 5 customers to have confirmed purchases when only 4 items were in stock.

## Identifying the Vulnerability

The design document explicitly states: "No lock or transaction spans the read and the write." This means:
1. Each checkout thread reads stock independently
2. Writes back happen as separate operations
3. Multiple threads can read the same value before any of them write

This is a classic **lost-update race condition**.

## Constructing the Attack Trace

**The key insight:** All 5 customers read stock level q4 before any write happens. Then they all write back q3 (their computed value), but since writes are sequential:
- c1 writes q3, stock goes q4 → q3 
- c2 writes q3, stock goes q3 → q3 (no further decrement!)
- c3, c4, c5 do the same (stock stays q3)

Result: 5 holds created, but stock shows only q3. Once all holds are established, all payments succeed at tick t0 (holds are still active).

## Event Sequence

```
(read-1 c1 q4 q3)
(read-1 c2 q4 q3)
(read-1 c3 q4 q3)
(read-1 c4 q4 q3)
(read-1 c5 q4 q3)
(write-stock c1 q4 q3 q4 t0)
(write-stock c2 q4 q3 q3 t0)
(write-stock c3 q4 q3 q3 t0)
(write-stock c4 q4 q3 q3 t0)
(write-stock c5 q4 q3 q3 t0)
(pay c1 t0)
(pay c2 t0)
(pay c3 t0)
(pay c4 t0)
(pay c5 t0)
```

**Final state:** All 5 customers are (sold ...), violating the invariant that sales ≤ stock (5 > 4).
